item.title: Yuri and I used to play football together. Then I spotted his name among Russia’s war dead
item.description:
I had no idea he had gone to fight in Ukraine and without hacked data I would probably never have learned of his death

One evening, after weeks spent counting Russia’s war dead, I began looking for names I might recognise.

My colleagues and I had been working our way through more than 11m death certificates leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, and identifying nearly half a million Russian soldiers who had died in the war in Ukraine.

item.title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
item.description:
Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed him

They are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals.

But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault, 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company.

item.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy criticises Trump for calling Putin his ‘friend’; Kyiv deploys new laser weapon
item.description:
Ukrainian leader likens Putin to Hitler; laser system intercepts Russian drone but not ready for ‘mass deployment’. What we know on day 1,739

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticised Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin his “friend”, likening the Russian leader to Adolf Hitler. “Of course it’s up to the president of the United States, but ... it’s strange,” the Ukrainian leader told the BBC in an interview aired on Friday. “He is an aggressor, and a killer... He can’t be a friend. Just cannot be. It’s the same that somebody says about Hitler during the second world war, that he’s a good friend. No. He’s not a friend.” Zelenskyy said what was needed was “more progress” and urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow.

Ukraine has for the first time used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered drone, according to its state-backed defence group Brave1. An adviser to Zelenskyy, Serhiy Beskrestnov, published footage earlier this week showing a target crashing in a fireball, saying a Russian Geran jet drone had been shot down by a laser system for the “first time”. Agence France-Presse quoted Brave1 as saying on Friday: “Footage recently emerged online showing a Ukrainian laser system being used in combat to intercept an enemy jet-powered drone.” The weapon was developed by a recipient of a Brave1 grant and operated by a private air defence team, Brave1 added. But it cautioned that “a first successful interception does not mean the technology is ready for mass deployment”. “Laser air defence remains an experimental technology,” it said, adding that at least seven teams in Ukraine were currently working on laser weapons. Beskrestnov said the system, known as Blysk and developed by the Ukrainian company Carmine Sky, was protecting critical infrastructure during the interception.

A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya has turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank ⁠a Russian naval warship in Benghazi ⁠port last Sunday, Reuters quoted ​three people from military and security services as saying on Friday. The convoy, which was escorted by the Russian navy frigate Golovko, turned around near the strait of Sicily on the same day as ⁠the attack in Benghazi, said a European military official who had been tracking the convoy. A Ukrainian military intelligence official and a Middle East security official confirmed the flotilla had turned from heading to Libya. Russia’s defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Ukraine has offered ⁠a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food ⁠exports and ⁠passed this ​on to international allies, the foreign minister ⁠said. “We are ready for ⁠a ceasefire. We are ​grateful to ‌India, Turkey and ‌Egypt, which are playing ‌an active and important role in de-escalating tensions in the Black Sea, as well as in mediation efforts. ‌We are now awaiting a response from ​Russia,” Andrii Sybiha was cited by public broadcaster Suspilne as saying on Friday. He added that Russia had proposed ⁠Ukraine suspend attacks on the ​Russian ​oil sector under ​the truce, but ​Kyiv ‌would only consider ​this ​as part of a bigger energy ceasefire deal.

Ukraine’s military said on ⁠Friday it ⁠had struck ​a Russian solid ⁠rocket fuel production site ⁠in ​the Tula ‌region south ‌of Moscow ‌overnight. “The plant is the starting point of the ‌missile production chain: it manufactures ​components for plastic explosives and ⁠the polymer used ​to produce ​solid ​propellant for ​Russian ‌ballistic missiles,” ​the ​defence ministry said on Telegram.

Russia’s foreign ministry has accused ⁠Latvia of creating artificial ⁠obstacles ⁠to hinder the ​transit of Russian grain to ⁠global markets, saying the restrictions pose additional risks ⁠to global food security. Ministry ​spokesperson ‌Maria Zakharova ‌claimed in a statement published ‌on the ministry’s website on Friday that Latvia was conducting inspections of Russian grain shipments for allegedly ‌stolen Ukrainian agricultural products and was seeking ways ​to ban Russian grain transit altogether.

item.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
item.description:
Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved

In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.
